name: Data.goodForms_inf_eigenPart_eq_bot
summary: Take pi projecting to the q-part and killing the other eigenparts of V'. On goodForms(V') pi is 0 (its image lies in the q-part of the good forms of V', which is 0), so 1 - pi has determinant 1 there, hence (equal determinants) nonzero determinant on goodForms(V); but 1 - pi kills the q-part of goodForms(V).

steps.claim: Choose pi in heckeAlgebra(D) acting as the identity on q-parts and as 0 on the d-parts for the finitely many other d with nonzero d-part on V'. Let y lie in goodForms(D, V) and in eigenPart(D, V, q); it suffices to show that 1 - pi is injective on goodForms(D, V) and kills y.

D.goodForms V ⊓ D.eigenPart V q = ⊥ := (D.exists_hecke_proj_eigenPart q

  Subtype.ext (sub_eq_self.2 (e.le ⟨(D.heckeOnGood _ π z).2, mem_comap.1 (((iSup_ne_bot_subtype
  _).trans (iSup_eigenPart ..)).ge.trans (iSup_le fun d v a ↦ by
  simpa [h d, a, top_inf_eq, ite_mem] using (· ▸ a)) ⟨⟩)⟩))))).trans_ne (by simp))).ker ⟨y, a.1⟩
  (Subtype.ext (sub_eq_zero.2 (by simp [h q _ y a.2])))).1)

steps.claim: 1 - pi acts on goodForms(D, V) with nonzero determinant: by det_heckeOnGood_eq its determinant equals that on goodForms(D, V'), where 1 - pi is the identity.

steps.claim: On goodForms(D, V') pi is 0: for z there, pi z is a good form (Hecke operators preserve good forms) and lies in eigenPart(D, V', q), since principalForms(D, V') is the sum of its nonzero eigenparts and pi maps each into the q-part; by the hypothesis pi z = 0, so (1 - pi) z = z.

  simpa [h d, a, top_inf_eq, ite_mem] using (· ▸ a)) ⟨⟩)⟩)))))

steps.claim: Hence the determinant is 1, nonzero, and 1 - pi is a linear equivalence of goodForms(D, V); its kernel is 0.
(1 - pi) y = y - y = 0, because pi is the identity on the q-part; so y = 0.
